A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChinaTravel and its NeSy Planning baseline. Text extraction and visual inspection of all 45 v4 pages and 53 v5 pages, including appendices, support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark evaluations, preference experiments, and DSL/POI error analyses in Table 3, Figures 4–8, and Appendix H.

after.justification: v5 retains original benchmark results and reports additional reasoning-model, English-language, ablation, and composition-complexity experiments in Tables 16–20.

M1.justification: The DSL primitives, NL2DSL refinement, search algorithm, and planning prompts remain unchanged. Rule-based choices newly displayed in Figure 5 were already described in v4 Appendix F. v5 Appendix D.8 illustrates possible extensions rather than establishing implemented new components.

E1.justification: v5 adds evaluated English versions of Easy-300 and Human-154 (Appendix H.6) and end-to-end planning comparisons across TripPlanning and TravelPlanner (Table 14), broadening linguistic and task coverage. Medium results concern an existing dataset tier; the renamed Intent Grounding task matches v4's POI Reasoning task.

E2.justification: The principal Act/ReAct, TTG, and LLM-modulo comparator families remain. v5 additionally evaluates DeepSeek-R1 as an Act comparator and introduces random-ranking controls. The separate GPT-4o/DeepSeek-V2.5/Qwen2.5-7B POI comparison in v4 Appendix H.2 is removed.

E3.justification: v5 adds a Pareto win-rate metric for the existing paired-preference scenarios while retaining rank aggregation. Additional experiments introduce R1/R1-Distill configurations, random-ranking controls, and evaluation stratified by composition complexity. Existing NeSy and TTG search budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds an isolated POI-ranking ablation, composition-complexity analysis, English-language checks, city-distribution analysis, and Pareto-based preference analysis. It removes v4 Appendix H.2's category-specific POI error breakdowns. The original single-preference and 15 paired-preference experiments are retained.

E5.justification: The existing LLM-modulo dispersion reporting is retained, without new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance procedures. Figure 8b's added points represent preference combinations rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: v5 adds substantial results in Tables 5, 14, and 16–20 and Figure 8b, while removing v4's older POI error results. Table 3 changes DeepSeek-V3 one-shot ReAct's Easy macro EPR from 6.25 to 6.00 and FPR from 5.42 to 5.33. It also swaps the Llama/Mistral icons on two oracle rows, changing their reported attribution without explanation.

T1.justification: v5 introduces explicit definitions for pairwise Pareto scoring, including ties, and composition complexity as the number of basic concepts in a DSL requirement. The existing DSL operators, pass-rate equations, and TTG mathematical formulation remain unchanged; no new proofs are supplied.

C1.justification: The central benchmark, compositional DSL, and NeSy findings remain. v5 drops the abstract's explicit 'first' novelty assertion and makes fixed constraint verification and insufficient NeSy evaluation more explicit contribution motivations. The introduction changes its illustrative success rate from 27.9% to 37.0%, already reported elsewhere in v4.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations concerning language-independent difficulty, the contribution of POI ranking, R1 overthinking, and DSL extensibility. It explicitly discusses the absence of RL post-training and associated resource/trajectory limitations. Older model-specific explanations of Chinese-context performance are removed with v4 Appendix H.2.

D1.justification: v5 adds project/code/dataset links, a supplementary-code reproducibility statement, collection dates, and institutional approval/consent disclosures. Core implementation details and prompts were already documented. New CC BY-NC-SA wording in Appendix J.5 conflicts with the retained CC BY-NC license in Appendix I.

R1.justification: v5 substantially expands positioning around the limitations of slot filling and compositional natural-language interaction. New cognitive-compositionality and compositional-learning references support this framing, alongside newer planning work such as SETS and ATLAS. The earlier general LLM/NeSy/travel discussion in Appendix C is largely retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the benchmark and results narrative are rewritten. Terminology shifts from POI reasoning toward intent grounding. Ethics moves into the main text, reproducibility and LLM-use statements appear, and the appendices are reorganized.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 5 are substantially redrawn, Figure 7's labels and legend are redesigned, and Figure 8 gains a Pareto panel. Seven tables are added, v4 Figures 13–14 are removed, and numerous retained tables, examples, and questionnaires are relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: v4 lacked English validation and an isolated POI-ranking control; v5 adds both, alongside reasoning-model and complexity-stratified tests, strengthening empirical diagnosis. The benchmark and headline findings remain stable. Sparse protocol/uncertainty detail, conflicting licensing statements, and unexplained Table 3 attribution changes temper these gains, supporting a useful but limited overall improvement.
